description: Bayesian fault isolation settings (card M3-05, idea text I-05). Signatures: configs/diagnose/signatures/<engine_id>.json (CALIBRATED). FMECA: docs/reliability/fmeca.json (MIL-STD-1629A style, ANUMAAN-authored).

fmeca_map.ref: ANUMAAN mapping of the registry faults (configs/faults.json) onto the FMECA modes by failure mechanism; null = no FMECA mode covers it (default occurrence used)

default_occurrence.ref: FMECA occurrence (1-10) for faults no FMECA mode covers

nominal_log_odds.ref: prior log odds of 'no fault' against the strongest single fault hypothesis while an alarm is active (alarms can be false: the model must earn its call)

window_frames.ref: exponential averaging of the residual z-vector before isolation (frames)

residual_var.ref: variance (z^2) of the averaged residual per channel: model error is correlated in time, so averaging removes only part of it

severity_max.ref: upper bound of the uniform prior on fault severity relative to the signature (severity 1)

sensor_bias_max_z.ref: bound of the uniform prior on a single-channel sensor offset (z units)

ambiguity_cosine.ref: signatures this collinear cannot be told apart: reported as one ambiguity group

min_posterior.ref: hypotheses below this posterior are not published

shared_sensors.ref: D61: channels derived from ONE physical sensor (every vibration order comes from the engine accelerometer's spectrum) share one sensor-fault hypothesis: a bad accelerometer shifts all its orders together, so a single raised order is evidence of a mechanical fault (bearing, gearbox, prop, mount), not of a sensor offset. Key = sensor name, value = channel-name prefix.

ecu_report_posterior.ref: D62: an ECU self-test report (e.g. a lane lost, Rotax OM-912 i p.4-5 warning indicator) is direct evidence, like a fault code; kept below 1 for a faulty report
